descriptive_title: Kindergarten Mathematics: Demonstrations — Spatial Sense and 2D/3D Shapes (A9.1-A9.7)
subject: Mathematics

curriculum_expectations.A9.3: use positional language (above, below, beside, inside, outside)
curriculum_expectations.A9.7: use shapes in art and patterns

unit_overview: A 5-day Kindergarten unit on spatial sense (A9.1-A9.7) framed around 'Shape Safari' — Sammy the Safari Sloth and Mira the Map-Making Monkey. Day 1 explores 2D shapes. Day 2 explores 3D shapes. Day 3 introduces positional language. Day 4 composes and decomposes. Day 5 closes with a shape art capstone. Each lesson includes an expanded_walkthrough.
unit_learning_goal: Children will identify, describe, and compose 2D and 3D shapes; use positional language; and apply shapes in art.

lesson_arc.big_idea: 2D shapes are FLAT. Circle, triangle, square, rectangle, hexagon. Each has a name and properties.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can identify and describe 2D shapes.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Sammy hunts 2D shapes around the safari; children identify and name shapes.

lesson_arc.big_idea: 3D shapes are SOLID. Sphere, cube, cylinder, cone, pyramid. They have faces, edges, vertices.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can identify and describe 3D shapes.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Sammy and Mira find 3D shapes; children compare to 2D shapes.

lesson_arc.big_idea: Positional words describe LOCATION. Above, below, beside, inside, outside, between.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can describe location with positional words.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Mira makes a treasure map; children use positional words.

lesson_arc.big_idea: Bigger shapes can be made of smaller shapes. 2 triangles = a square. We build (compose) and break (decompose).
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can compose and decompose shapes.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Children compose larger shapes from smaller ones; build 3D structures.

lesson_arc.big_idea: Shapes are everywhere — in art, animals, buildings. We use shapes to make pictures.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can use shapes to make a safari picture and describe it.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Children create a safari picture using 2D shapes; describe it with positional language.

recurring_characters.name: Sammy the Safari Sloth
recurring_characters.role: Lead character. A friendly sloth wearing a safari hat. Anchors all 5 lessons.
recurring_characters.visual_description: A young sloth in safari hat with binoculars and a backpack. Slow smile, hanging from a branch.

recurring_characters.name: Mira the Map-Making Monkey
recurring_characters.role: Sammy's partner. The 'positions' character — makes maps and gives directions. Cameo Lessons 3-5.
recurring_characters.visual_description: A young monkey with a map, compass, and pencil. Eager expression, holding the map.

threaded_vocabulary.child_friendly_definition: Flat shapes — like a piece of paper.
Solid shapes — like a real ball or block.
To put together. 2 triangles compose a square.

pedagogical_notes: Kindergarten spatial work is concrete and play-based.
2D and 3D distinction must be hands-on with real objects.
Positional language is foundational — use throughout the day.
Compose/decompose lays groundwork for fractions and area later.
canadian_context_notes: Canadian shape examples: maple leaf (irregular), Olympic rings (circles), hockey rink shape (rectangle), Canada coin shapes.
Safari animals popular in Canadian children's books.
Use snowflakes (hexagons) as a Canadian winter shape connection.
